profile: Explicit cooperative ownership only; no opaque-host hard preemption

cases.recipe: Create operation; its first acquire starts a synchronous resource; inspect actual context cleanup registration before start.
Acquire start throws the exact fixture object synchronously before producing a resource; close operation and scope.
Admit a cooperative pending acquisition; start close; observe admission closed and close pending; resolve resource; hold its asynchronous release; then release the gate.
Admit a cooperative acquisition, begin close, then reject acquisition with the fixture Error. Observe both caller-facing acquisition rejection and cleanup without unhandled rejection.
Create exactly three close waiters: direct close, registered invocation cleanup, and finally-close, while one release is gated. All waits remain pending until that release finishes.
From an admitted cleanup callback, try acquire, child, and registerCleanup on the closing operation; attempt another write after close.
Register three cooperative releases: first throws, second waits on a host gate, third succeeds. Closing must still drain the second and third.
Caller signal is already aborted with a unique object before operation creation/admission. No resource callback may start; public rejection keeps that same object.
Graph parent admits two children. Parent close begins while one child release is gated; new parent and child acquisitions are refused before callbacks.
Normally close left child; right child subsequently writes 72696768740a before parent closes. Closing left must not abort right or parent.
Two Shell instances share a host-owned resource provider with separate leases. Abort one invocation while the other continues and writes 7369626c696e670a.
Use explicit child(destination) for a graph-owned operation; independently create another operation from a write-only forwarded output. Do not infer parentage from hidden capability metadata.
Caller abort, selected execution rejection, and cleanup rejection all occur at controlled barriers. Public exec/dispose drain resources and preserve the caller object.
Without caller abort, execution rejects while cleanup also rejects. Repeat with an Error, false, zero, and undefined rejection reason; distinguish rejection state from truthiness.
Command fulfills exitCode7, then cooperative cleanup rejects with the exact fixture Error. A nonzero result is not an execution rejection and must not hide cleanup failure.
Command fulfills exitCode7 and cleanup succeeds. Close is normal, not an invented caller abort or EPIPE.
Caller aborts an unenrolled opaque host command before its promise rejects. Public settlement must not await that opaque promise; after settlement reject it and observe the process rejection channel.
Destination exposes legacy write and ownedOutput.write with separate counters. An enrolled operation writes 00ff and 41620a; exactly the accounted route is used.
Actual Shell output limit5 admits two writes 00ff and 41620a; limit4 rejects before publishing the over-limit second write. Capture and external sink see identical charged bytes.

Actual cat consumes nonzero-byteOffset Buffer views reused only after awaited writes/producer advancement: 00ff410a then 4200fe0a. Poison original views after finalization; do not require an extra return after ordinary EOF.
Direct enrolled copy uses a gated destination write and a structural producer. While the first write is pending no second next is allowed; resolve writes and finish normally.
Create and close an operation without invoking acquire or write. Enrollment alone must not activate a producer or issue an empty probe write.
Nested public invocation shares maxOutputBytes3: inner writes 4142, outer attempts 4344. The second operation must not reset or double-charge the shared budget.

With stdout consumer already closed, curl -o /work/body -D /work/headers -w '%{http_code}\n' performs one authorized transfer. Body, headers, upload and cleanup remain required; only stdout publication is canceled.
Actual curl stdout-only transfer begins; downstream closes after its first accepted payload. Response disposal and owned request close finish before public exec/dispose settle.
Close an enrolled stdout operation while a separate stderr destination and file operation remain live. They write literal bytes 646961670a and 66696c650a.
Actual cat starts one admitted cooperative VFS source. After downstream closes, release that source and do not open the second operand. No extra read may be added to trigger lifecycle behavior.
Injected authorized transport must receive upload chunk4100ff0a before the producer is allowed to yield4200fe0a/EOF. Reuse the first backing Buffer only on advancement. No complete-input staging.

An injected transport deliberately consumes exactly the first upload chunk then supplies a completed early response without requesting the remaining tail. A following command reads tail from the shared structural cursor; final invocation close owns its single return.
Caller aborts while a declared cooperative request acquisition is pending; it then yields an owned response/request. Await disposal and request close, preserve caller reason, and publish no payload.
Host maxRedirects0/maxRetries0, CLI -L and a302 response pointing at another origin. Permit only the initial authorized request; no target authorization or upload replay.
Host maxRedirects0/maxRetries0, CLI -f --retry3 and a503 response with Retry-After. Do not retry, wait for retry, or replay upload.
First origin redirects to an allowed second origin, then to a denied third. Observe stripped credentials on the actual second request, and policy denial before acquiring the third transport.

Task-owned loopback HTTP server and actual createNodeHttpTransport stream to a finite downstream. Independently witness client request close and server connection cleanup before shell settlement; no external service or native curl.
Legacy write-only ByteSink, no ownedOutput and no optional context cleanup hook. Explicit helper use must preserve awaited writes and normal result without inventing capability metadata.

An unenrolled opaque async input remains pending in next when its return is requested. Capture the unchanged pending/finalizer behavior; release it through the same host gate, not a timeout-based success.
